methods.label: Pair opposite sectors
methods.explanation:
For any fixed column, the shaded squares occupy either the odd-numbered rows or the even-numbered rows. It is therefore useful to compare the probabilities of choosing these two types of rows.

The three diameters drawn in the wheel form the opposite-sector pairs \((1,9)\), \((2,6)\), and \((3,7)\). Within each pair, the sectors have equal central angles because these are vertical angles. Thus the two sectors in each pair have equal probabilities on a random spin.

Dividing the numbers in these pairs by \(5\) gives the respective pairs of row remainders
\[
(1,4),\qquad (2,1),\qquad (3,2).
\]
Each pair contains one odd row and one even row. The pairs cover every wheel sector exactly once, so the total probability of an odd row equals the total probability of an even row. Each probability is therefore \(\frac12\).

The first-spin remainders are all among \(1,2,3\), so every first spin selects a displayed column. Because the spins are independent, whichever column is selected, the second spin has probability \(\frac12\) of choosing its shaded rows. The requested probability is \(\boxed{\frac12}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
